title: Add TP stress scenarios to perf-canary (long context, bursty concurrency, replica churn)
creator: Kira Volkov
description:
Context
- TP hangs/timeouts under sustained mixed workloads are showing up as p99 blowups and occasional Sev1s. We currently lack a perf-canary signal that reliably exercises the failure modes (long context + mixed prefill/decode + bursty concurrency + replica churn).
- Goal is not to produce an exhaustive benchmark suite, but to add a small set of deterministic-ish stress scenarios that (a) reproduce known stall signatures more often than baseline traffic sim and (b) act as regression guardrails for runtime-1.19 TP fixes.

Scope
Add TP stress scenarios to perf-canary that run continuously (or scheduled) against a TP-enabled runtime build:
1) Long-context stress (prefill-heavy): large prompt lengths to push scheduler/comms ordering + KV behavior.
2) Bursty concurrency (mixed prefill/decode): short spikes in concurrent streaming requests with mixed prompt lengths.
3) Replica churn: intentionally drain/restart a replica during load to verify watchdog/abort semantics and ensure we don’t wedge the whole pool.

Non-goals
- Model quality evaluation.
- Full coverage of every GPU type; we’ll start with A100/H100 TP configs used by Dedicated and the busiest Hosted clusters.

Proposed scenarios (v1)
A) tp_long_context_prefill
- Config: TP=4 (A100 80GB baseline), context distribution p50=16k, p90=32k, p99=48k; decode 128–256 tokens.
- Traffic: steady-state QPS tuned to ~70–80% target utilization to leave headroom for variance.
- Expected failure mode coverage: NCCL collective ordering mistakes; stream sync regressions; KV pressure issues.

B) tp_bursty_mixed_streaming
- Config: TP=4, mixed prompt lengths (1k–16k) with 20–30% long prompts; streaming enabled.
- Traffic: bursts every N seconds (e.g., 20s burst, 40s idle-ish) to stress queue/backpressure; include client cancellations to exercise abort/cancel paths.
- Expected failure mode coverage: scheduler starvation, cancellation-related deadlocks, timeout storms under burst.

C) tp_replica_churn_under_load
- Config: TP=4, moderate prompt lengths (2k–8k), continuous load.
- Churn action: drain + restart a single replica once per run window (guarded) OR roll a pod if running in the canary environment.
- Expected failure mode coverage: watchdog-triggered drain behavior, alert noise/dedupe, safe fallback routing, preventing “wedged pool” behavior.

Metrics + thresholds (initial; adjust after 3–5 days of baseline)
Primary reliability gates
- Request timeout rate (tp canary routes):
  - WARN: >0.20% over 15m
  - PAGE: >0.50% over 15m OR any single run with >2.0% timeouts
- Hang/stall detectors (from ENG-4823):
  - PAGE: any replica with TP heartbeat gap > 30s for >=2 ranks OR stall_reason_count{reason in [collective_wait, stream_sync_wait]} > threshold baseline*3
- Replica drain events (watchdog / safety abort):
  - WARN: >2 drains per hour in canary cluster
  - PAGE: >5 drains per hour OR drains correlated with increased customer-visible timeouts

Performance regression gates (soft gates initially)
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency by scenario vs trailing 7-day baseline:
  - WARN: p99 +15% sustained over 30m
  - BLOCK RELEASE (after baseline stabilized): p99 +25% sustained over 30m (excluding known GPU maintenance windows)
- Throughput (tokens/sec per replica) under tp_long_context_prefill:
  - WARN: -10% vs baseline
  - BLOCK RELEASE (later): -15% vs baseline

Notes on baselines
- First week: thresholds are advisory while we collect stable baseline; still page on clear hangs/heartbeat gaps (these should be near-zero even in baseline).

Alerting + routing
- Alerts owned by Eng Serving Runtime + SRE.
- Paging route: #eng-sre on-call (primary) + #eng-runtime (secondary) during runtime-1.19 canary windows.
- Runbook linkage: Confluence runbook “runtime-tp-hang-mitigation” (once published) should be the first link in alert annotations.

Implementation plan
1) Define scenario configs in perf-canary repo (YAML/JSON) with explicit TP topology + workload distributions.
2) Add canary runner hooks to support burst patterns and controlled churn action.
3) Emit scenario tags in traces/metrics so we can slice by scenario (required for debuggability).
4) Add dashboards panels + alert rules for new scenario metrics; wire annotations back to this ticket.
5) Run for 3–5 days, calibrate thresholds, then mark as release gating for runtime-1.19.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] perf-canary includes at least 3 new TP scenarios (long context, bursty mixed streaming, replica churn) and they run in the canary environment without manual intervention.
- [ ] Scenario runs are labeled/tagged so timeouts/heartbeats/drains can be attributed to a specific scenario.
- [ ] Alert rules exist for (a) request timeouts and (b) TP heartbeat gaps / stall reasons; alerts link to dashboard + runbook.
- [ ] Baseline data collected for >=72 hours with a written “threshold calibration” note in the ticket.
- [ ] On regression: scenario fails the canary gate and posts actionable logs/links (run id, replica id, rank ids, stall reason) for triage.

Dependencies / coordination
- Depends on ENG-4823 for stall detector metrics + naming stability.
- Coordinate with SRE (Aisha Bello / Sergio Costa) for alert policy and noise limits.
- Coordinate with Rina Kobayashi on repro harness overlap to avoid duplicating effort.

Links

- Instrumentation: ENG-4823
- Perf-canary PR (draft): https://github.com/perf-canary/pull/188
- Observability dashboards PR (draft): https://github.com/observability-pack/pull/412
comments: 2025-02-20 (Marcus Reed): Drafted 3 scenario definitions; starting with TP=4 A100-80GB because it matches Acme Dedicated incidents. Need to confirm we can safely do replica churn in canary without impacting other runs; may need a dedicated namespace/cluster.

2025-02-22 (Aisha Bello): For paging, prefer heartbeat-gap based alerts over raw timeout spikes (timeouts can be noisy during deploys). Suggested: PAGE on heartbeat_gap>30s + stall_reason=collective_wait; WARN on timeout_rate>0.2%. Please ensure scenario_tag is added to both logs and metrics so we can filter out non-TP routes.

2025-02-25 (Rina Kobayashi): Repro harness has a similar long-context config; recommend aligning prompt length distribution so failures are comparable across perf-canary and benchmark-lab. Also please include client cancellation to cover the disconnect deadlock signature.

2025-02-28 (Marcus Reed): Implemented burst pattern runner and scenario tagging. Replica churn still WIP; proposing a 'controlled drain' API call in canary harness rather than directly restarting pods. Will post updated PR today; will start collecting baseline once merged.
